sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul, Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2015. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 18th ed., entry 'Naga, Tangkhul [ntx]'. Dallas: SIL International (Internet Archive copy 2018-09-17).
sources.note: Nothing (no typology field). Gives location (Somra tract, south Layshi township; Homalin township), 4,000 speakers (2004 SIL), dialect note ('Somra village is the prestige dialect'), lexical similarity 31% with [nmf], 51-52% with Akyaung Ari [nqy], 29-32% with Koki [nxk]; Latin script based on Somra; Bible 1989.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2011. Change Request Number 2011-064: split of [nmf] into Naga, Tangkhul (India) [nmf] and Naga, Tangkhul (Myanmar) [ntx] (adopted 2012-02-03). Dallas: SIL International. 5 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Basis of the split is an unpublished sociolinguistic survey by Myanmar researchers (fieldwork 2004, report 2010: wordlists + questionnaires in 3 Tangkhul (Myanmar) villages); 31% lexical similarity with Ukhrul Tangkhul; separate Somra-based orthography/literature. Cited published sources are ethnographic (Saul 2005, Stirn & van Ham 2003, Tin Yi 2004, Min Naing 1960) plus Burling 2003.

sources.note: No descriptive item on Somra/Myanmar Tangkhul found (only ethnographic/historical mentions of the Somra tract; Matisoff 1995 Languages and Dialects of TB lists 'Somra' as a Kuki exonym for the Tangkhul in Burma). Search engines, Google Scholar, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, CrossRef, HathiTrust, sil.org and ethnologue.
